# ob-12 — Detect symlink and hard-link aliases between input, output, and manifest

**Findings:** Obfuscator/FileWrite.cs: SamePath compares Path.GetFullPath case-insensitively only; a symlinked or hard-linked path to the same file is not rejected · **Size:** S · **Tree:** core

Not in this slice: hard-link detection (no native file-identity interop) and bind mounts.

## Why

FileWrite.SamePath compares Path.GetFullPath strings only. A symlinked directory component can make the output path name the input file; with --force, the rename-based publish then replaces the real input with the obfuscated output and the original is lost. Hard links are out of scope: outputs are staged and renamed into place, so a hard-linked input keeps its original inode and content.

## Files

Obfuscator/FileWrite.cs; Obfuscator.Tests/ObfuscatorTests.cs; README.md.

## Failing tests

Obfuscate with --force where the output path reaches the input through a symlinked directory: throws, and the input is unchanged. Obfuscate with --force where the manifest path is a symlink to the input file: throws. Deobfuscate with --force where the output reaches the manifest through a symlinked directory: throws, and the manifest is unchanged. Skip symlink tests where the OS refuses to create the link (for example, Windows without the privilege).

## Implement

Before comparing, SamePath canonicalizes each path. It resolves symlinks in every existing component, starting at the root. It resolves each link with FileSystemInfo.ResolveLinkTarget(returnFinalTarget: true) and rebases relative targets on the link's directory, then appends the components that do not exist yet unchanged. The case-insensitive compare stays. Hard links are not detected. README states that symlinks are resolved and that hard links are not, with the reason.

## Check

Run the new symlink tests and the existing alias tests, then dotnet test Obfuscator.slnx and scripts/test-local.sh. Check that a normal round trip under a symlinked temp directory (for example, /var -> /private/var on macOS) still succeeds.
